function.description: Execute a REAL bridge. SPENDS REAL FUNDS AND IS IRREVERSIBLE: it signs and broadcasts a deposit from the user's wallet on the source chain. APPROVAL: over MCP in a restricted project the call WAITS until the user answers the card in Vex, and that card IS the confirmation - do not ask for another in chat. It returns the settled outcome: executed (reported as this tool's own status, confirmed or confirmed_unrecorded), declined, expired, refused, dispatch_failed or indeterminate; never call it twice while you wait and never retry an indeterminate one. In a full project it executes directly under the user's standing permission. Run BridgeQuote first. That quote authorizes THIS tool whichever venue it chose; BridgeQuoteRelay authorizes only BridgeExecuteRelay. PRECONDITIONS, each refused BY NAME: a fresh BridgeQuote on the SAME provider, identical params, within 15 minutes. Resolve fromToken and toToken separately with TokenFind, each with exactly one target chain, continuing only when mutationReady is true; ambiguous, provider-capped or metadata-unreadable results are not executable identities. `amountRaw` decimals come from that contract-verified candidate: a provider-list decimal is not signing authority. The approval card shows each exact chain, token contract, contract-read symbol and decimals, and the human and atomic source amounts. The route, the refund address and the destination are derived from the source and the selected destination wallet; a caller-supplied `refundTo`, `referrer`, `referrerFeeBps`, `routeId`, `depositMethod` or `recipient` is rejected by name, and `fromAddress` redirects nothing: the session wallet signs only for itself. Venue: Khalani's live registry picks Khalani when it serves both sides, Relay otherwise (how Robinhood Chain routes). Vex charges 25 bps of the input token as a separate transfer after the deposit lands. IT NEVER REPORTS SUCCESS: a broadcast deposit is not a delivered bridge; every arm says do NOT re-bridge. Full contract: vex_ToolDescribe.
function.name: BridgeExecute

amountRaw.description: Amount in raw atomic units of fromToken (e.g. USDC has 6 decimals, so 1 USDC = "1000000"). Read decimals from a contract-verified TokenFind candidate on the exact source chain. A provider-list decimal is not signing authority, and a raw amount without contract decimals is unsafe. A raw amount next to a token whose decimals you have not read is a thousandfold error waiting to happen.
